preparer.emits: RPA 3 text (claims + 3 blocks), request.json = the claims array + the point claim, receipt preparation.json

reformulation: Row-addition only: no variable, bound, integrality marker, objective coefficient, RHS or original row changes. 20,484 L rows 'sum_{e in C} x[e,k] - 2 c_k <= 0' are added, one per induced five-cycle C (5,121) and label k in {0..3}. The integer feasible set is preserved exactly (each cut is the implied odd-cycle bound sum_{e in C} x[e,k] <= 2 c_k) and the target LP is a strict subset of the source LP (the fractional witness violates odd5_1_0 by 1/2).

shape.graph: 12,288 vertices, 18,431 edges, 12,286 degree-3 + two degree-2, 1,023 bridges, 1,024 blocks of 12 vertices, 5,121 induced five-cycles

request_3mb_answer: 3,030,310 B request = 3,030,250 B claims + 38 B point claim. Each of the three claims is 1,010,08x B and 1,009,973 B of it (99.99%) is the same literal identity projection [[i,i] for i in range(73728)]; a claim's own content is five scalars (reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective, inverse), with inverse 1 / 0 / null. The cut family contributes zero request bytes: the 20,484 rows live in target.mcm (14,767,168 B) and their derivations in proof.rpa blocks[0]. proof.rpa re-embeds the identical claims block (3,030,250 B) and adds three 73,728-entry identity Return maps (26,400,323 B of the 50,933,002 B of blocks), so 29,430,323 of 54,405,699 B (54.1%) is identity-coordinate bookkeeping rather than mathematics. The complete-coordinate bijection is semantically required for the strictness point claim (crates/core/src/point.rs:186-198), so a shorthand must expand to the same checked object rather than weaken it.
cut_family_template_answer: Yes, measurably: all 20,484 derivations collapse to a single JSON shape family - base Lin (kind Le, 10 terms = 5 RowUpper + 5 VarLower), Int Lin (5 terms), Cases (6-term target expression, left branch 1 step, right branch Lin+Round+Lin) - one shape for all 20,484 instances, differing only in 15 integer indices (activation, 5 cycle vars, 5 spoke lower bounds, 5 source rows). Hand-expanded they cost 24,582,620 B of steps (2.66 KB per instance); a template plus per-instance parameters would carry the same family, and the 256 MiB text cap (which binds at about 101,000 hand-expanded instances of this shape) stops being the scaling wall. docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:380 states shared affine/mapping DAGs and dedicated batch records 'are not implemented by this wire layout', so today this exists only as a Python loop.
claims: Forward source->target integer claim: same coordinate set on both sides (projection [i,i] over all 73,728 vars), input_integers=output_integers=true, objective Equal, inverse=1; 61,452 steps and 456,708 obligations = 73,728 VarLower + 73,728 VarUpper + 73,728 VarInt + 49,152 RowUpper + 18,431 RowEq + 20,484 Local (one per added cut row, discharged by the Cases derivations in the same block) + 147,457 Exact (full inverse identity).
Reverse target->source integer claim (inverse=0): 436,224 obligations and 0 steps - every target row is either an original source row or a Local fact already derived in the forward block.
Reverse target->source LP claim (input_integers=false, inverse=null): 288,768 obligations, 0 steps; the 73,728 VarInt obligations disappear.

Strictness point on inclusion claim 2: 73,728 rational coordinates (442,409 B in proof.rpa) built from the audit recipe (activations 1; cycle 1/2; spokes 0; other edges 1/4; the other three labels (1-a)/3), violating odd5_1_0 by 1/2 while satisfying all 67,583 source rows and 73,728 bounds.
No row or variable is deleted anywhere, so both reverse directions are step-free: the reformulation is pure row addition and the forward block carries all 61,452 derivation steps.
proof_encoding: RPA 3, 54,405,699 B = claims 3,030,250 + blocks 50,933,002 + points 442,409; assembled RPX 35,810,749 B; verify execute_us 803,549 / 810,474 on the two recorded runs, with byte-deterministic reassembly.

Blocks: [61,452, 0, 0] steps. Per cut exactly 3 top-level steps: Lin (base, 5 RowUpper + 5 VarLower refs at coefficient 1/2), Lin (kind Int, 5 VarInt refs), Cases (binary split on the activation; right branch = Lin with (5/2)*VarUpper, Round, Lin with 2*Assumption).
End sections 26,400,323 B (9,615,707 / 9,283,353 / 7,451,263) holding three 73,728-entry identity Return maps (one Expr per coordinate) plus 1,181,700 obligation refs: 456,708 / 436,224 / 288,768.

Obligation composition (forward): 20,484 Local refs are exactly the added rows; RowUpper 49,152 + RowEq 18,431 = the 67,583 source rows, so the format directly exercises 'added row discharged by a local fact' at scale.

Negative checks: four in-place mutations (drop a spoke nonnegativity term, swap an Int premise, drop one inverse coordinate, set the witness to -1) each assemble (exit 0) then verify (exit 2); the recorded INVALID results carry only status+message ('obligation mismatch: expected Le', 'rounding premises', 'missing obligation', 'strictness witness is not feasible in the inclusion output LP').
agent_manual_work: Hand Fraction MPS parser for both the 23 MB and 29 MB files (sections NAME/ROWS/COLUMNS/RHS/BOUNDS/ENDATA, markers, one or two row/value pairs per record), then a hand-written MPS writer inserting 20,484 L rows inside the existing COLUMNS groups plus a second independent row-oriented readback parser; original and final SHA-256 recorded.

Structure recovery from complete coefficient incidence, not names: each E row = one edge with its four label assignments, every assignment sits in exactly one E and two L rows under the same activation, four activations share the same vertex support collection; 12,288 vertices, 18,431 edges, degrees 3/2, no parallel edges.
Bridge/block analysis by iterative DFS (1,023 bridges, 1,024 blocks of 12 vertices, contracted path) with 17,408 independent internal-edge deletion connectivity checks as a second certification.

Two independent exhaustive five-cycle enumerations (length-5 adjacency walks with canonical ordering; every 5-subset of every block with induced degree 2) agreeing on 5,121 cycles, plus a 64-pattern local binary truth table and an exact fractional witness checked against all 67,583 rows and 73,728 bounds.

In the preparer: re-verified every audit record against both models (target-minus-source row set equals the 20,484 cuts, coefficient vector equals the intended expression, five distinct source rows, activation binary with bounds [0,1]) and rebuilt the 73,728 witness coordinates coordinate by coordinate (tools/prepare_test66.py:62-77).
preparer_helpers: SparseBuilder.lin (tools/prepare_test70.py:14) - untrusted exact accumulator that merges refs into one residual, asserts it equals the wanted expression and emits one Lin step; 3 top-level steps per cut.

cases_le_shared (tools/prepare_test70.py:32) - shared-lookup Cases emitter with per-branch child builders; referenced by 11 preparer files under tools/ (one definition plus a copy in prepare_test70_subset_global.py).
rounded (tools/prepare_test84.py:15) - Round emitter that computes the exact ceiling of the integer-residual constant; used 20,484 times here.

expression / expr_json / row_fact (tools/prepare_test40.py:72,81,87) and parse_mps / row_ref (tools/prepare_affine.py:20,77) - algebra, fact-ref and MPS vocabulary; the preparer re-parses both MPS files although the same run canonicalises them to source.mcm/target.mcm.

remove_term / wrong_integer / missing_inverse / invalid_point (tools/prepare_test66.py:110-124) - four hand-written mutation recipes with undo closures, re-encoded into throwaway RPAs by execute() (:99-105).
friction: The RPA is 20,484 repetitions of one 3-step derivation, with no batch/template or shared-DAG form available (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:380); 24,582,620 B (45.2%) of the file is that repetition, produced by a hand-written loop.

3,030,310 B of request text encodes five scalars per claim: the identity projection is listed 73,728 times per claim (3 x 1,009,973 B), restated inside proof.rpa claims, and restated again as three 73,728-entry Return maps.

The obligation list is mirrored by hand (tools/prepare_test66.py:14-31: per-coordinate VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt loops, one ref per output row, then 'Exact'*(1+n+n) for the inverse identity); nothing reports the plan the verifier will expect, so counts are re-hard-coded in the receipt (:79).

Family discovery ran entirely in eval Python: the two five-cycle enumerations, the bridge/block census and the failed all-cubic-leaf probe, which died with 'min() iterable argument is empty' because no cheap structural query exists.

Edit attribution lives outside the certificate: the only binding of an added row to its five witness rows is untrusted audit.json (13,472,440 B), which the preparer must re-verify field by field before it may be trusted.
notes: No resource friction: the RPA is 54.4 MB (21% of the 256 MiB text cap), assembly 0.38-0.40 s, verify ~0.81 s, no RESOURCE_LIMIT. The case is the pure row-addition shape - 0 steps in both reverse claims - so the compiler work is entirely (a) enumerating the family, (b) deriving each added row locally, (c) restating same-coordinate identity obligations, which is exactly where the format is verbose today. The receipt's own capability census shows branches=20484 with every lift counter at zero: this case exercises Lin/Int/Round/Cases only.
